surprises.description: Welltower raised the 2026 normalized FFO guidance midpoint to $6.50, above the preview’s base-case expectation of a $6.44–$6.48 midpoint and its $6.50+ bull case threshold. The increase was larger than the preview’s expected modest raise.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Welltower raised its full-year 2026 FFO guidance midpoint by $0.10 to $6.50 per share.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base (55%) … FY nudged to ~$6.44–$6.48”; “Bull (25%) … FY raised to ~$6.50+.”

surprises.description: SHOP same-store NOI grew 21%, above the preview’s estimated 18–20% range and at the high end of the company’s prior full-year guidance range. The preview said a result with a “2” handle would be a clear beat, though it also described a 20%+ quarter as the whisper expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “21% growth in the senior housing operating (SHOP) portfolio,” its “16th consecutive quarter of SHOP same-store NOI growth exceeding 20%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “SHO SSNOI growth ~18–20% (est.)”; “anything with a ‘2’ handle is a clear beat”; “the 16th straight 20%+ quarter is the whisper.”

surprises.description: Q3 normalized FFO of $1.67 per share beat the $1.64 consensus estimate by $0.03, a modest beat that also reached the preview’s bull-case range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 normalized FFO was $1.67 per diluted share.”

surprises.description: Revenue growth of 38% exceeded the preview’s expected 35% year-over-year growth, implying revenue above the cited $3.63–$3.66 billion consensus range.

SHOP expenses rose only 4.3%, with ExpPOR up 80 basis points, well below the preview’s base-case expectation of 1.5–2.5% and below its 2% checkpoint. Margins expanded 310 basis points, but the 31.7% margin was slightly below the preview’s 32% threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “SHOP same-store OpEx grew only 4.3% (ExpPOR up just 80 bps), expanding margins 310 bps to 31.7%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “ExpPOR drifts to 1.5–2.5%” in the base case; catalyst checklist: “ExpPOR ≤2% and NOI margin ≥32%.”

surprises.description: SHOP flow-through reached a post-COVID high of 66%, and management said rate-driven revenue growth carries essentially no associated cost. The preview watched the RevPOR/ExpPOR spread but did not anticipate this level of flow-through or this explicit rate-versus-cost characterization.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The SHOP flow-through margin reached a post-COVID high of 66%,” with management emphasizing “rate-driven revenue carries essentially no associated cost.”

surprises.description: Year-to-date investment activity rose to $21 billion from the $15.5 billion reported at Q2, while the company acquired less than 3% of screened assets. Much of the remaining activity was sourced off-market and more than half involved sellers taking Welltower units as partial consideration, details not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Year-to-date investment activity reached $21 billion across 196 granular transactions”; “acquired less than 3% of assets screened”; “Nearly 85% of the remaining $7.7 billion of activity was sourced off-market and more than 50% involved sellers taking Welltower units as partial consideration.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “$15.5B pro rata YTD investment activity at Q2”; preview said to watch “new announced volume” and “equity funded vs. leverage.”

surprises.description: The Q3 acquisitions included SHOP communities bought at a 10–15% discount to replacement cost and skilled nursing deals at roughly 9% rent yields. The preview focused on deployment volume and funding but did not set expectations for these deal terms or yields.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 acquisitions included 43 SHOP communities … bought at a 10-15% discount to replacement cost, plus ~$850 million of skilled nursing deals at ~9% rent yields.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Capital deployment pace and funding mix” was a key metric to watch; the preview cited prior acquired assets averaging six years old and ~75% occupancy.

surprises.description: Welltower received full repayment of its $130 million Genesis senior secured term loans when Genesis completed Chapter 11, bringing its total IRR on Genesis investments since 2011 to nearly 9%. This repayment and investment outcome were not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Wellower received full repayment of its $130 million Genesis Healthcare senior secured term loans upon the company's Chapter 11 completion,” bringing total IRR “to nearly 9%.”
